question: does the segmented scheme, verified in numpy, also work on the device?
change: evolve_torch now splits the integration at the regime switches from _event_times and takes a uniform dlna inside each segment, forcing the last step of every segment to land on the boundary. Added a dlna override so the step can be chosen per run.
verdict: THE DEVICE PATH NOW PASSES ON BOTH CORRECTNESS AND ACCURACY.
accuracy: 0.111% at dlna = 0.002, against the 0.5% requirement - a 4.5x margin. It is marginally better than the numpy segmented run at the same setting (0.154%), which is floating-point ordering, not a different scheme.
correctness: rhs_torch is bit-identical to the numpy rhs (0 of 229 state rows disagree) after porting the two missing massive-neutrino masks, so this accuracy is not being bought by a wrong operator.

what_is_still_not_there.speed: 616.88 s at T=1 is far slower than numpy on one trajectory, and that is expected rather than a defect: the break-even table puts T=1 at 0.08x. The device path only wins at T >= 16384, where the rhs alone measured 3.76x (15.68 ms vs 59.03 ms).
what_is_still_not_there.no_batched_entry_point: nothing constructs the T=16384 batch this needs, and power.matter_power still runs bucket_by_k=True, i.e. T=1, the worst possible size.
what_is_still_not_there.no_end_to_end_number: there is still no device-vs-CPU comparison of the full nonlinear pipeline, so no GPU speedup may be quoted yet.
what_is_still_not_there.scope_of_the_accuracy_result: one cosmology, one wavenumber (k=0.05 /Mpc), three state variables (dc, db, dg), z=0. No k sweep and no P(k).

why_the_two_halves_now_fit: the earlier dead end was that a single uniform grid over the whole a-range cost 2.2% and refining it hit a 1.29% floor, while adaptive control needs a host decision every step and would have destroyed GPU batching. Segmenting at the switches resolves both at once: the host synchronises once per segment (five here) instead of once per step (thousands), and inside a segment the whole batch advances on a plain fixed grid - which is exactly the regime where the measured 3.76x applies.
next_step: build the batched entry point: assemble 128 cosmologies x 128 wavenumbers as one T=16384 batch, run the segmented device integrator over it, and compare the full nonlinear pipeline against the CPU path at 16/32/128 - that is what the acceptance criterion actually asks for.
contradiction_with_the_task_list: M2b is recorded as 'CUDA backend (generated kernels, device-resident batched evolution) + hardware validation (completed)'. Measured: git ls-files | grep -ci cuda returns 0, no module imports any backend, rhs_torch was wrong on 48 of 229 rows until fixed this session, and the shipped integrator was 2.2% inaccurate with a fixed step over the whole range. There was no CUDA backend and no hardware validation.
